title: Elements in Array After Removing and Replacing Elements
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, elements are removed from the start of the array every minute until the array is empty, and then elements are appended back in the order they were removed.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, elements are removed from the start of the array every minute until the array is empty, and then elements are appended back in the order they were removed. This cycle repeats indefinitely. For each query specified by queries[j] = [timej, indexj], determine the value at indexj in nums at minute timej. If indexj is out of bounds for nums at timej, return -1. Return an array ans of size n where ans[j] is the result of the j-th query.
constraints: During minutes zero through n, remove one element from the front per minute; during the next n minutes, append removed elements in original order.
The state repeats every 2*n minutes, with an empty array at phase n.
For each [time,index], return that current element or -1 when the index is absent.
hints: Only the time modulo the full remove-and-rebuild cycle matters.
Before phase n the array is nums[phase:]; after phase n it is nums[:phase-n].
Check whether index is within that phase length and map it to nums[index+phase] or nums[index].
The formulas directly describe the exact elements remaining or restored at every phase.
editorial: The formulas directly describe the exact elements remaining or restored at every phase.

tests.explanation: The queried states give two, two, absent, and zero respectively.
The one-element cycle alternates between [5] and empty.
